tasks.short: Consult engineers about customer product problems and agree the technical response.

steps.what: Retrieve product specifications, order details and previous technical cases.
Ask the customer for operating conditions, symptoms and missing measurements.
Assemble a technical brief with evidence and unresolved questions.

loop.input: Customer correspondence, problem evidence and linked case records.
loop.output: A technical brief separating observations, hypotheses and missing evidence.
loop.check: Require source references, preserve measurements and units, and flag contradictions for representative review.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved contradictions return to the representative.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text symptom descriptions need synthesis; templates alone cannot reliably preserve their meaning.

steps.what: Discuss possible causes, tests and customer constraints with the engineer.
Approve the technical disposition and any limits on customer advice.
Record the approved disposition and assign follow-up actions.

tasks.design: Link product and order records in the {CRM} to specifications in the {DOCS} and transactions in the {ERP}. A bounded drafting loop prepares a source-linked technical brief; a structured engineering disposition triggers case updates and follow-up actions through the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Problem evidence sits across correspondence, technical documents and transaction records. Engineering decisions often arrive as informal messages.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record links and forms handle retrieval and follow-up. AI-assisted coding can reduce connector work, while a bounded model loop handles the free-text brief.
tasks.still_hard: Reproducing intermittent faults, distinguishing misuse from product defects and approving advice with safety implications.
tasks.human_edge: The representative understands the customer's situation; the engineer takes responsibility for technical interpretation and advice.

ambition.what: A structured technical issue review for customers with repeated unresolved faults.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time assembling evidence and chasing actions. They can lead customer issue reviews, with technical approval held by the engineer.

reach.task: Prepare a fault investigation and test plan.
reach.learn: Failure modes, measurement quality, operating limits and escalation criteria.

evidence.claim: Record retrieval, structured dispositions and follow-up routing can use existing configuration; free-text briefing benefits from bounded drafting.
Technical diagnosis and approval remain human responsibilities; implementation ranges and remaining time are planning estimates.

assumptions: The baseline represents a mid-size European manufacturer or distributor with internal or supplier engineering support.
Time shares cover all participating roles within this task and are estimates informed by the supplied priors.
The engineer can record a disposition in a structured form.
GDPR access restrictions apply to customer contacts and correspondence.
unknowns: Whether product, order and case identifiers match across records.
Who may approve technical advice and safety-related actions.
Whether supplier engineering records can be accessed.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed changes.
research_questions: Which missing measurements most often cause a second engineering consultation?
Can the configured case view retrieve the necessary evidence without a custom connector?
new_work: Review draft briefs and correct unsupported interpretations.
Resolve missing identifiers and conflicting specifications.
Maintain technical brief templates, access rights and engineering escalation rules.
Audit whether approved dispositions reach the correct case.

tasks.short: Sell environmental technical products by matching customer needs to supported performance and commercial terms.

steps.what: Discuss the customer's process, environmental objectives, constraints and buying criteria.
Compare product specifications and select a technically suitable option.
Calculate operating costs and environmental performance against the customer's current approach.
Prepare a proposal with product scope, evidence, pricing and assumptions.
Check claims, commercial limits and assumptions before sending the proposal.
Explain trade-offs, address objections and negotiate within delegated limits.
Forward the accepted proposal and agreed terms to the order desk.

tasks.design: Configure a product and quotation flow across the {CRM}, {ERP} and approved evidence in the {DOCS}. Deterministic selection rules and calculators produce comparisons and proposals; the {WORKFLOW} gates customer release and routes accepted terms to the order desk.
tasks.previous_blocker: Product compatibility, environmental evidence and pricing are maintained separately. Bespoke comparisons require repeated manual assembly.
tasks.enabler_now: Configurators and quotation templates already support rule-based selling. AI-assisted coding can make product-specific calculators and connections cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Reliable environmental comparisons need defensible boundaries and customer operating data. Unusual applications and unsupported claims require technical review.
tasks.human_edge: The representative discovers the real buying criteria, explains uncertainty and negotiates commitments the supplier can meet.

ambition.what: Smaller customers needing a documented operating-cost and environmental comparison.

tasks.altitude: The representative can prepare more evidence-backed options during the sales conversation. Commercial decision rights remain within existing delegated limits.

reach.task: Validate product suitability for a customer's operating conditions.
reach.learn: Compatibility rules, performance boundaries and interpretation of test evidence.

reach.task: Convert accepted terms into a complete order request.
reach.learn: Item identifiers, delivery conditions and order completeness checks.

evidence.claim: Product configuration and quotation can connect to finance and customer records.
A vendor case reports that quotation preparation fell from about 15 minutes to 90 seconds; this does not establish savings for the complete sales task.
Environmental calculators need explicit baselines, units and assumptions; negotiation remains human work.

assumptions: The baseline concerns business customers buying technical equipment or materials.
A manageable initial product family has approved compatibility rules and current evidence.
Existing quotation configuration is available; otherwise the artefact generator needs deterministic code.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies to customer contact records; national rules govern any required employee consultation.
unknowns: Whether environmental claims have approved supporting evidence and comparison boundaries.
Whether customer operating data is reliable enough for calculations.
Which discounts, warranties and performance commitments require additional approval.
Whether accepted terms arrive in structured form or need manual reconciliation.
Whether the existing quotation module supports the required product rules.
research_questions: Which product family has the cleanest rules and evidence for an initial release?
Can the existing quotation configuration enforce compatibility and approval limits?
Which assumptions most often change the customer's preferred option?
new_work: Maintain product rules, price versions and approved environmental evidence.
Check calculator outputs when factors or operating assumptions change.
Review proposals and route exceptional commitments to the authorised approver.
Reconcile accepted proposals with negotiated changes before order handoff.

tasks.short: Visit customer establishments to understand product sales and agree account actions.

steps.what: Review account purchases, previous visits and outstanding account actions.
Arrange a visit and request available establishment sales figures.
Travel to the customer establishment.
Inspect product availability, presentation and local selling conditions.
Discuss sales trends, stock movements and customer feedback with establishment staff.
Reconcile establishment sales figures with shipments and previous reports.
Enter visit findings and assign agreed account actions.

tasks.design: Configure an account brief and mobile visit form in the {CRM}, with purchase history from the {ERP}. Where customers provide structured sales reports, a deterministic connection through the {DATA_PLATFORM} produces comparisons in the {BI}; the visit form records observations and assigns account actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier shipment records do not reveal the establishment's sales to its customers. Local conditions and informal explanations are gathered during visits.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured mobile forms remove duplicate entry. Available customer reports can be mapped and checked with small deterministic integrations.
tasks.still_hard: Customers may not share detailed sales data. Physical availability, local behaviour and candid explanations still require observation and relationships.
tasks.human_edge: The representative notices context missing from reports and earns useful explanations from establishment staff.

ambition.what: Weekly replenishment follow-up for accounts supplying current sales reports.

tasks.altitude: Visits still dominate the week, but account preparation and reconciliation shrink. The representative can initiate replenishment discussions within existing account responsibilities.

reach.task: Identify accounts needing intervention from sales and stock signals.
reach.learn: Seasonality, channel stock movements and the difference between shipments and customer sales.

reach.task: Check replenishment requests against item and delivery records.
reach.learn: Product mappings, pack sizes and delivery cut-offs.

evidence.claim: Account briefs, mobile records and structured sales comparisons can use configuration and deterministic integrations.
Shipment history cannot establish customer sales without stock or sales evidence; site observation and discussion remain substantial.

assumptions: The establishment resells the products and the visit includes travel.
Some customers provide aggregate product sales reports; no access to individual consumer or patient records is assumed.
No visit is eliminated in the remaining-time estimates.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies to contact records; employee monitoring changes require assessment under national rules.
unknowns: Which customers share establishment sales and stock reports.
Whether reports use consistent products, periods and pack sizes.
How much travel is already shared with other account tasks.
Whether offline access is needed at customer sites.
Whether proposed visit records change employee monitoring and require consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which discrepancies can be explained by returns, transfers or reporting periods?
Can existing mobile forms work reliably at the establishments visited?
Which account actions become useful when reports arrive between visits?
new_work: Maintain customer product mappings and report schedules.
Resolve missing reports and unmatched sales lines.
Keep visit forms short and maintain access to customer records.

tasks.short: Explain product energy efficiency and environmental impact using customer-specific evidence and assumptions.

steps.what: Find current specifications, test evidence and approved environmental claims.
Calculate customer-specific energy use and environmental comparisons.
Build presentation material with comparisons, sources and limitations.
Check comparison boundaries, evidence and claims before authorising customer use.
Present the evidence, explain uncertainty and answer customer questions.
Send supporting material and route unanswered technical questions.

tasks.design: Use a versioned evidence library in the {DOCS} and deterministic calculators on the {DATA_PLATFORM} to generate source-linked presentation material. The {WORKFLOW} records technical approval and prepares the customer evidence pack, while the {CRM} tracks unanswered questions and follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence is scattered across specifications and presentations. Reusing slides can silently carry old factors, unsupported wording or incompatible comparison boundaries.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned evidence, standard claim wording and template generation handle most preparation without a model. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building calculators and document generation.
tasks.still_hard: Customer-specific operating assumptions and environmental comparisons may remain uncertain. New claims need technical interpretation and defensible evidence.
tasks.human_edge: The representative makes uncertainty understandable and recognises when a question exceeds the approved evidence.

ambition.what: A customer operating-scenario workshop comparing energy use under alternative conditions.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends more preparation time testing scenarios and less time rebuilding slides. They can lead scenario discussions within approved technical boundaries.

reach.task: Explain performance sensitivity to operating conditions.
reach.learn: Functional units, comparison boundaries, uncertainty and sensitivity analysis.

reach.task: Demonstrate product performance using an agreed test protocol.
reach.learn: Repeatable demonstrations, measurement limitations and interpretation of observed results.

evidence.claim: Approved claim libraries, deterministic calculations and presentation templates can automate preparation without generating new technical claims.
Technical review and interactive customer explanation remain necessary for unfamiliar assumptions and unsupported questions.

assumptions: The baseline concerns a tailored customer presentation, with engineering review of its technical comparisons.
The evidence library contains structured metadata and approved wording for the initial product family.
The calculator reuses the same comparison calculation as the environmental product sales task.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies to customer-specific records; national rules determine any employee consultation requirement.
unknowns: Who approves environmental claims and presentation variants.
Whether supporting evidence is current, comparable and cleared for customer distribution.
Which operating factors the customer can supply reliably.
Whether existing presentation templates can be populated automatically.
Whether the proposed records change employee monitoring or require consultation.
research_questions: Which approved comparisons cover the most common customer questions?
Which assumptions materially change the result and should be visible during the presentation?
Can technical review focus on changed claims and assumptions while retaining traceable approval?
new_work: Maintain evidence versions, approved wording and calculator factors.
Review changed assumptions and new claims before customer use.
Check generated charts, units, sources and document rendering.
Route unsupported questions to engineers and add approved answers to the evidence library.

role.altitude: The role remains centred on customer conversations, site observation and technical judgement. Less preparation and record handling creates room for evidence-backed comparisons and structured account reviews; broader technical or commercial authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: Sales engineer: prepare clearer technical investigations and explain operating sensitivities.
Sales manager: turn account sales signals into specific intervention proposals.
Order clerk: produce complete, traceable order requests from accepted terms.
Demonstrator: connect product demonstrations to approved measurement evidence.
skills_to_grow: Technical problem framing and measurement quality.
Customer sales analysis and stock interpretation.
Evidence-backed negotiation and clear technical explanation.
role.ambitious_version: Become a technical account adviser who helps customers diagnose problems, compare operating scenarios and plan account actions using traceable evidence. Build this capability around shared product rules, calculators and case records.

job.title: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing, Technical and Scientific Products
